title: Allen Bradley Kinetix 6000
op_body_verbatim:
Hi everyone,

I'm troubleshooting an Allen-Bradley Kinetix 6000 Integrated Axis Module at our plant.

Existing unit:


Catalog number: 2094-AC09-M02-S
Series: A
Replacement unit:


Catalog number: 2094-AC09-M02-S
Series: C
The catalog number is exactly the same; the only difference is the series revision.

When we install the Series C unit, it does not operate. On one occasion, the internal fuse soldered directly to the amplifier PCB blew.

I'd like to know:


Has anyone successfully replaced a Series A unit with Series C using the same catalog number?
Are there any hardware revision or firmware compatibility issues we should consider?
Could a defective replacement unit or another internal fault explain the blown PCB fuse?
Are there any known issues with this particular model?
We have stopped powering up the replacement because of the blown fuse.

Any advice or experience would be greatly appreciated. Thank you!


Daniel from Philippines

Is a Series A to Series C swap of the same catalog number supported, are there hardware-revision or firmware compatibility issues to check, could a defective replacement or another fault (bus/power rail, wiring) explain the blown PCB fuse, and are there known issues with this module?
